reviewed_state: Frozen published snapshot; no production mutation

scope.supporting_code: text/walk, playlist_metadata/completion, load_initial/load_next, reduced fixture construction; six fixture/manifest JSON files; crawl_manifest.json

invariants: Only the actual primary-list continuation is admitted; outer and unrelated action targets are excluded.
Every admitted list entry preserves its video ID, order, source position and appearance multiplicity.
A failed, malformed, cyclic or capped traversal cannot silently claim successful exhaustion.
Supported Renderer and ViewModel controls retain compatibility.

findings.title: Missing primary-list target can match an unaddressed response action
findings.invariant: A continuation response must be bound to the positively identified primary-list target; missing identity must not be treated as an equal identity.
findings.observed_code: initial_list returns container.get(targetId) without validating it. continued_list accepts item.get(targetId) == target, so two missing values compare equal.
findings.counterexample: A selected modern itemSectionRenderer contains one video and a valid continuation control but omits targetId. The next response contains one appendContinuationItemsAction without targetId and another video. With a declared total of two, crawl_one admits the action and reports exhausted_reconciled, pagination_exhausted=true, count_reconciled=true, target_id=null.
findings.smallest_repair: Require a nonempty string target before following any pending continuation, and reject a missing/invalid target at the continued_list boundary. Preserve a valid terminal single-page list if no target is needed.
findings.focused_verification: Run the missing_primary_target synthetic case. It must return an explicit error/incomplete result with the existing pending continuation retained, never exhausted_reconciled. Retained playlist replay must remain unchanged.
findings.data_impact: Synthetic malformed/unsupported input only. All ten selected real playlists have nonempty targets, and all 22 retained pages replay exactly; no published count discrepancy is demonstrated.

findings.title: Malformed legacy continuation controls are silently treated as terminal
findings.invariant: A recognized list-continuation container that cannot supply a usable token must remain an explicit parse gap instead of disappearing from the queue.
findings.observed_code: parse_list appends legacy nextContinuationData.continuation only when truthy and silently ignores every other supplied legacy control.
findings.counterexample: parse_list receives one valid video and legacy_continuations=[{nextContinuationData:{}}]. It returns the video and an empty pending list without error. completion with declared=1 reports exhausted_reconciled and pagination_exhausted=true, although a malformed continuation control was present.
findings.smallest_repair: Validate every supplied legacy continuation object. Accept the supported nextContinuationData shape only with a nonempty string continuation; reject missing tokens and unsupported legacy control shapes with a concise ValueError. Do not guess how a reload control should paginate.
findings.focused_verification: The malformed_legacy_continuation case must raise a parsing error; a supported nonempty nextContinuationData token must still be returned and followed. Re-run the retained-page and existing reduced-fixture checks.
findings.data_impact: Synthetic malformed input only. This shape was not encountered in the retained selected playlist pages; no present inventory row or count is shown to be wrong.

verdict_scope: Two fail-closed parser repairs before unrestricted reuse. The observed pagination correction and the published selected-playlist counts are supported by retained-response replay.
exclusions: No live network refetch or new public-video content review.
No verification of private/unlisted/deleted availability or channel snapshot freshness.
No complete review of scope classification, transcript matching, workbook construction or publication code.
The two counterexamples are malformed-input risks, not observed production-data failures.
